To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the design of low power microsystems requires a system-level approach and the development of a design flow and respective design technology which allows to predict the low-level ramifications of high-level design decisions.
the system architect should have access to a power estimation tool which is able to estimate the power of a design at the algorithm- and architecture level.
the system architect should have a tool that allows him to estimate the power consumption of his design at the architecture level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of design technology which allows the design of low power digital systems in a predictable and efficient way.
the development and application of methods and tools for a system-level design methodology which is able to predict power consumption of a design before the implementation phase.

the development of an EDA tool chain for low power design which enables system designers to predict the power consumption of their design at an early design stage and to optimize it in a pre-implementation design space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a system-level design technology for low power systems has been successfully developed.
the presented design methodology is a promising approach to reduce time-to-market of complex systems.
we can now design predictable low power systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a new design flow for low-power systems can be established, which enables the system architect to estimate the impact of his decisions before the time-consuming and tedious RT-level implementation starts.
we have developed a methodology for system-level low power design and have developed the tools to implement it.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to design low power systems with a predictable power consumption and a predictable design effort.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a design methodology which is based on pre-implementation estimation, optimization and design-space exploration is a key to success for predictable design of low power SoC's.
the design flow and the EDA support tools are mature enough to be used for real world design projects.
the design flow for low energy consumption systems is different from conventional design flows.
